title: Start named virtual threads and wait for them

blocks.text: Java 21 builds virtual threads with the `Thread.ofVirtual()` builder. The builder can name every thread it makes: `name("http-handler-", 0)` names the first thread `http-handler-0`, the next `http-handler-1`, and so on. Virtual threads are always **daemon** threads, so nothing keeps the JVM alive for them: whoever starts them must wait for them, and a thread that may never finish is joined with a timeout.

items: `startAll(String prefix, long first, List<Runnable> tasks)` starts one **virtual** thread per task and returns the started threads in task order. The thread for `tasks.get(i)` is named `prefix + (first + i)`.

`awaitAll(List<Thread> threads, Duration limit)` waits for the threads, but never much longer than `limit` in total, and returns the threads that are still alive when it stops waiting (in their list order; empty when all finished). It stops as soon as every thread has ended. Mind `Thread.join(long millis)`: `join(0)` means "wait for ever", so a deadline turned into whole milliseconds can become an endless wait (the tests cannot force that moment, so it is not graded).

rows: two started virtual threads, `job-7` running `a` and `job-8` running `b`
`awaitAll(threads, 6 s)`, each thread runs for about 2 s
`[]`, after about 2 s, all threads finished

cases.says: startAll starts one thread per task and every task runs.
awaitAll returns an empty list when every thread has already finished.
awaitAll really waits: threads that run for 2 s have all finished when it returns within a 6 s limit.
Every thread startAll returns is a virtual thread.
The threads are named prefix + first, prefix + (first + 1), ... in task order.
awaitAll stops waiting at the limit and returns the thread that is still running.
With five stuck threads and a 1 s limit, awaitAll returns after about 1 s in total, not 1 s per thread.
awaitAll returns as soon as every thread has ended, not after sleeping out the whole limit.
The limit is one shared deadline, not split evenly: with 4 threads and 4 s, a thread that takes 2 s is still waited for.

concepts: A builder's name(prefix, start) names each thread it makes, counting up from start.
A thread that may never finish is joined with a timeout, so the caller is never blocked forever.
Thread.ofVirtual() and Thread.startVirtualThread() create virtual threads, and isVirtual() tells a virtual thread from a platform one.
